# Adjudication Task — Chapter 253

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃253화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|쉭!
  6|
  7|기수식(起手式) 따위는 없었다. 비무의 시작을 알리는 깃발이 올라가기 무섭게 두 사람은 서로를 향해 쇄도했다.
  8|
  9|그리고 십여 장의 거리가 순식간에 좁혀진 그 순간, 유운신룡의 허리춤에서부터 휘황한 빛줄기가 솟구쳤다.
 10|
 11|‘시작부터 검기를?’
 12|
 13|모든 것에는 장단점이 있는 법.
 14|
 15|검기는 강력한 힘을 발휘하는 대신, 공력 소모가 극심하다.
 16|
 17|유운신룡은 이번 비무에서 장기전이 아니라 속전속결을 택했다.
 18|
 19|슈와악!
 20|
 21|그의 송문고검(松紋古劍)에서 흘러나온 푸른 기운이 청풍의 어깨를 향해 내리그어진다.
 22|
 23|군더더기 없는 일격. 아마 유운신룡이 처음 검을 잡았던 날부터 수없이 휘둘렀던 궤적이었을 것이다.
 24|
 25|하지만…….
 26|
 27|‘내 눈에 보인다는 건, 청풍에게도 마찬가지라는 거지.’
 28|
 29|쾅!
 30|
 31|딱 반걸음 차이. 푸른 검기에 휩싸인 송문고검이 비무대에 작렬했다.
 32|
 33|그러나 유운신룡은 풍부한 경험을 지닌 절정 고수. 그는 예상했다는 듯이 검을 비틀어 청풍의 발목을 베어 갔다.
 34|
 35|“아이코!”
 36|
 37|쉭! 쉬쉬쉭!
 38|
 39|잔망스러운 외침과 함께 검을 피해 낸 청풍이 몸을 뒤틀었다.
 40|
 41|이어서 검기가 맹수의 발톱처럼 사방을 할퀴고 갈라 낸다. 그 궤적에 걸려든 헐렁한 장포 자락이 갈기갈기 찢어져 흩날렸다.
 42|
 43|그 광경에 군중들 사이에서는 비명과 탄성이 흘렀다.
 44|
 45|“꺄악!”
 46|
 47|“헉!”
 48|
 49|하지만 내게는 똑똑히 보인다. 생채기 하나 나지 않은 청풍의 몸과 입가에 매달린 웃음이.
 50|
 51|녀석은 즐기고 있었다. 춤을 추듯 산들거리는 몸놀림으로 검격에서 벗어난 청풍이 활짝 웃으며 박수를 쳤다.
 52|
 53|“와아! 방금 그거 태청검법(太淸劍法)이죠?”
 54|
 55|“마, 맞소.”
 56|
 57|엉겁결에 대답한 유운신룡은 어안이 벙벙한 얼굴이었다.
 58|
 59|그뿐만 아니라 누구라도 그랬을 것이다. 이게 뭐야, 방금 저놈이 어떻게 피한 거지? 그런 생각들로 머리가 꽉 차 있을 것이 분명했다.
 60|
 61|“검로가 되게 재밌다. 혹시 태극혜검(太極慧劍)은 안 익히셨어요?”
 62|
 63|“그건 왜…….”
 64|
 65|“태극혜검을 꼭 한번 보고 싶었거든요. 할아, 아니 아는 분께서 몇 번 칭찬하셨어요. 좋은 무공이라고.”
 66|
 67|태극혜검은 나도 몇 번 들어 봤을 정도로 유명한 무당파 최고의 절기.
 68|
 69|청풍은 순수한 의도로 말했을 뿐이지만, 녀석의 캐릭터를 모르는 사람이 들으면 무례하기 짝이 없는 말이기도 하다.
 70|
 71|예를 들면 당장 눈앞에 있는 유운신룡도 마찬가지였다.
 72|
 73|“본문의 무공은 평가를 받기 위해서도, 그대를 즐겁게 하도록 존재하는 것도 아니오.”
 74|
 75|딱딱하게 굳은 얼굴로 말한 유운신룡이 자신의 송문고검을 들어 청풍을 겨누었다.
 76|
 77|“하지만 그토록 원한다면 보여 주지. 얼마나 무서운 무공인지.”
 78|
 79|부드럽지만 강대한 기세가 일어나 사위를 짓누른다. 동시에 검 끝이 천천히 움직이며 원을 그렸다.
 80|
 81|태극(太極). 무당파 무공의 진수가 지금 그의 손에서 펼쳐지려 하고 있었다.
 82|
 83|“태극혜검! 태극혜검이군요!”
 84|
 85|“부디 전력을 다하시오. 그렇지 않다면 후회하게 될 테니.”
 86|
 87|화아악!
 88|
 89|말을 끝마친 유운신룡의 신형이 허깨비처럼 사라졌다.
 90|
 91|다음 순간, 푸른 검기가 넘실거리며 청풍의 상반신을 노렸다.
 92|
 93|비무가 시작된 이래 단 한 번도 뽑히지 않았던 청풍의 검이 모습을 드러낸 것은 그때였다.
 94|
 95|쐐애애액, 쾅!
 96|
 97|검기와 검기의 충돌. 단 한 번의 격돌이었지만 우세는 명백했다.
 98|
 99|일 장을 주르륵 미끄러진 유운신룡이 눈을 부릅떴다. 찢어진 그의 손아귀에서 피가 흐르고 있었다.
100|
101|“이, 이게 무슨.”
102|
103|“이번에는 제가 가도 되나요?”
104|
105|물음과 함께 청풍의 신형이 허깨비처럼 흩어졌다.
106|
107|화산파의 암향표(暗香飄). 과거 녀석과 비무를 하며 지긋지긋하게 보았던 바로 그 움직임이었다.
108|
109|일 년이라는 시간이 흐른 지금, 그의 암향표는 더욱 은밀해지고 빨라져 있었다.
110|
111|쉭!
112|
113|유운신룡의 정수리를 베어 가는 검 끝에 엷은 자줏빛 기운이 서려 있다.
114|
115|피할 수 있을 만큼 최대한 피하고, 공격 시에는 그 순간만 검기를 사용하는 모습.
116|
117|불필요한 공력 소모를 줄이는 동시에 완벽하게 자신의 기운을 제어하고 있다는 증거였다.
118|
119|“헛!”
120|
121|대경한 유운신룡이 황급히 검을 쳐올렸다. 그러나 이번에는 조금 전과 달랐다. 송문고검이 청풍의 검신을 타고 흐르며 방향을 바꾼 것이다.
122|
123|유능제강(柔能制剛). 부드러움으로 강함을 제압하는 그것이야말로 무당파 무공의 근간이자 태극혜검에 담긴 묘리였다.
124|
125|하지만…….
126|
127|“어, 저도 비슷한 거 할 줄 알아요.”
128|
129|스으윽.
130|
131|천진난만한 말과 함께 청풍의 손목이 유연하게 회전했다.
132|
133|끈질기게 달라붙으며 청풍의 검신을 누르고 있던 송문고검이 단번에 맥없이 떨어져 나갔다.
134|
135|순간 허공에서 휘청이는 송문고검을 청풍의 검이 옭아맸다.
136|
137|“됐다. 이렇게 하는 거 맞죠?”
138|
139|“……!”
140|
141|“아닌가? 잠깐만, 이렇게 하면 더 잘될 것 같은데. 아, 이거구나.”
142|
143|갑자기 검을 거두고 골똘히 생각에 잠겨 있던 청풍이 환하게 웃었다. 반대로 그를 바라보는 유운신룡의 얼굴에는 경악이 가득했다.
144|
145|그리고 그것은 비무를 지켜보던 무림인들도 마찬가지였다.
146|
147|“으헉!”
148|
149|“태, 태극혜검을!”
150|
151|힘은 더 큰 힘으로. 부드러움은 더한 부드러움으로 제압된다.
152|
153|유능제강의 묘리를 무공의 근간으로 삼은 무당파, 그중에서도 최고의 절기라는 태극혜검을 같은 방식으로 제압했으니 그 놀라움은 대단했다.
154|
155|‘청풍이 유운신룡보다 한 수. 아니, 최소 두 수 앞선다.’
156|
157|그 사실을 직접 상대하는 유운신룡이 느끼지 못했을 리 없다.
158|
159|“도, 도대체 어떻게?”
160|
161|“음. 그냥 상대를 포용한다고 생각하면 돼요. 그럼 어디서 어떻게 움직여야 할지 몸이 저절로 반응해요. 참 쉽죠?”
162|
163|“…….”
164|
165|쉽겠냐. 미친놈아.
166|
167|아니, 그보다 정말 저렇게 할 수 있는 거야?
168|
169|‘일 년 동안 만두만 먹었다던 놈이.’
170|
171|내가 황당함에 물든 눈동자로 청풍을 바라보던 그때, 충격으로 눈꺼풀을 파르르 떨던 유운신룡이 돌연 청풍을 향해 달려들었다.
172|
173|츠츠츠!
174|
175|그 어느 때보다 환한 빛을 내뿜는 푸른 검기. 모든 공력을 끌어모은 일격이 틀림없다.
176|
177|금방이라도 가슴을 가를 듯이 다가오는 검날 앞, 멀뚱멀뚱 서 있는 청풍의 모습에 관객들의 비명이 터져 나온 찰나였다.
178|
179|쉬쉬쉬쉬쉭!
180|
181|선명한 자줏빛 광염(光焰)이 비무장을 가득 채웠다. 청풍의 손에 들린 검이 아름다운 궤적을 그렸다.
182|
183|그 한 번의 움직임만으로도, 나는 지금 청풍이 무슨 무공을 펼치고 있는지 알 수 있었다.
184|
185|‘매화삼십육검(梅花三十六劍).’
186|
187|그것은 더할 나위 없이 빠르고 부드러웠다.
188|
189|문득 코끝에 매화향이 스치는 듯했다. 자하신공의 자줏빛 검기가 꽃망울을 터트리고 서른여섯 개의 매화를 피워 올렸다.
190|
191|그리고 다음 순간, 유운신룡의 송문고검이 청풍의 가슴 앞에서 우뚝 멈췄다.
192|
193|쩌저적.
194|
195|방금 전만 하더라도 줄기줄기 쏟아지던 검기는 온데간데없다. 곧게 뻗은 새하얀 검신 위로 실금이 거미줄처럼 번지고 있었다.
196|
197|자신의 애검을 바라보던 유운신룡의 입술 사이로 힘없는 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
198|
199|“매화…… 그렇군. 화산파의 제자였구려.”
200|
201|화들짝 놀란 청풍이 말을 더듬었다.
202|
203|“아, 아닌데요.”
204|
205|“하긴, 뭐가 그리 중요하겠소.”
206|
207|체념, 그리고 납득.
208|
209|유운신룡의 팔이 스르륵 땅을 향해 내려갔다. 산산이 부서져 수백 개의 파편이 된 송문고검이 비무대 위를 뒹굴었다.
210|
211|“내가 졌소.”
212|
213|그제야 비로소 적막이 깨어졌다.
214|
215|정신을 차린 심사관이 깃발을 내렸고, 막혀 있던 둑이 터지듯 어마어마한 군중들의 함성이 사방을 휩쓸었다.
216|
217|
218|
219|* * *
220|
221|
222|
223|“저 어땠어요? 잘했죠?”
224|
225|천진난만한 목소리에 상념에서 깨어났다. 아이처럼 눈을 반짝이는 청풍이 코앞에 얼굴을 들이민 상태였다.
226|
227|“깜짝이야. 이런 것 좀 자제합시다.”
228|
229|“은인, 저 어땠냐니까요?”
230|
231|대답을 보채는 이 청년이 아까 그 사람 맞나 싶다.
232|
233|무적신검, 그는 무당파의 미래이자 십봉룡 중 한 사람인 유운신룡을 말 그대로 압살했다.
234|
235|그리고 이번 비무를 보며 다시 한번 깨달았다. 청풍은 이미 후기지수의 영역을 오래전에 뛰어넘었다는 것을.
236|
237|‘이 정도였나.’
238|
239|높은 고지에 올라서니 더 많은 풍경이 보인다. 청풍이라는 산도 마찬가지였다. 일 년 전의 나는 미처 보지 못했던 풍경이었다.
240|
241|‘대단하다. 순전히 타고난 재능이라는 것이 믿기지 않을 정도로.’
242|
243|일신에 지닌 무위도 놀랍지만, 재능만큼은 아니다.
244|
245|보고 있자면 시스템 사용자가 아닐까 의심이 들 정도로 청풍은 타고난 천재였다.
246|
247|“은인. 왜 대답을 안 하세요?”
248|
249|“어린앱니까? 그런 것까지 칭찬해 주게.”
250|
251|청풍이 약간 시무룩해진 얼굴로 중얼거렸다.
252|
253|“할아버지는 항상 말해 줬었는데…….”
254|
255|“그거야 그쪽 사정이고.”
256|
257|일부러 퉁명스레 대답한 그때였다.
258|
259|“이야, 비무 잘 봤네. 친구!”
260|
261|어디선가 불쑥 튀어나온 목소리에 청풍이 환하게 밝아진 얼굴로 돌아섰다.
262|
263|“종리추!”
264|
265|“오오, 기억하는군. 친구여!”
266|
267|“그럼, 당연히 기억하고 말고요. 아니 말고!”
268|
269|“…….”
270|
271|지랄들 한다.
272|
273|나는 서로 얼싸안고 하하 호호 웃던 종리추와 청풍을 가만히 지켜보다가 문득 떠오르는 생각에 입을 열었다.
274|
275|“잠깐. 거기 두 사람.”
276|
277|“응? 왜 그러나?”
278|
279|“왜요?”
280|
281|“서로 다음 비무 상대 아냐?”
282|
283|멀뚱멀뚱 서로를 바라보던 두 사람이 헉, 하고 숨을 삼켰다.
284|
285|“마, 맞아요!”
286|
287|“그, 그렇군. 내 다음 비무 상대가 강풍, 자네였어.”
288|
289|벌써 우정에 금이 가는 소리가 들리는구나.
290|
291|엉거주춤 서로에게서 떨어지는 두 사람을 보며 쯧쯧 혀를 찼다.
292|
293|‘뭐, 그래 봤자 결과는 대충 나와 있지만.’
294|
295|모든 것이 그렇듯 성라대연에도 운이라는 요소가 작용한다. 그런 의미에서 종리추는 천운을 타고난 놈이었다.
296|
297|어쩐 일인지 어중간한 이들과 연이어 붙으며 준결승까지 올라왔으니 말이다.
298|

“Hah!”

Softness overcoming hardness.

[P64]
But…

[P65]
“Oh, I know how to do something similar too.”

[P66]
*Shhk.*

[P67]

[P68]

[P69]

[P70]
“Got it. This is how you do it, right?”

[P71]
“……!”

[P72]
“Or not? Wait, I think it’ll work better like this. Ah, that’s it.”

[P73]
Cheongpung abruptly withdrew his sword and sank into thought. Then he smiled brightly.

[P74]
The Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon, on the other hand, stared at him in horror.

[P75]
So did every martial artist watching the duel.

[P76]
“Gah!”

[P77]
“T-The Taiji Wisdom Sword…!”

[P78]
Strength was overcome by greater strength. Softness, by even greater softness.

[P79]
Wudang had built its martial arts upon the principle of softness overcoming hardness, and the Taiji Wisdom Sword was its greatest supreme technique. Cheongpung had just defeated it through that very same principle.

[P80]
The shock was immense.

[P81]
*Cheongpung is one level ahead of the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon. No, at least two.*

[P82]
There was no way the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon, who was facing him directly, hadn’t realized it.

[P83]
“H-How did you do that?”

[P84]
“Hmm. You just have to think of embracing your opponent. Then your body reacts on its own and knows where and how to move. Easy, right?”

[P85]
“……”

[P86]
*Easy, my ass, you lunatic.*

[P87]
More importantly, was that really something a person could do?

[P88]
*And this is the guy who supposedly spent a whole year eating nothing but dumplings.*

[P89]
As I stared at Cheongpung in disbelief, the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon’s eyelids trembled from the shock.

[P90]
Then he suddenly charged.

[P91]
*Tzzzz!*

[P92]
Blue Sword Energy blazed more brightly than ever. He had clearly gathered every last bit of his internal energy into that one strike.

[P93]
The blade hurtled toward Cheongpung as if it would split his chest open. The spectators screamed at the sight of Cheongpung simply standing there—

[P94]
*Swish-swish-swish-swish!*

[P95]
Brilliant violet light-flames filled the dueling arena. The sword in Cheongpung’s hand traced a beautiful path through the air.

[P96]
That single movement told me exactly which martial art he was using.

[P97]
*The Thirty-Six Plum Blossom Swords.*

[P98]
It was supremely fast and smooth.

[P99]
For a moment, I could almost smell plum blossoms. The violet Sword Energy of the Zaha Divine Technique burst into bud, blooming into thirty-six plum blossoms.

[P100]
The next instant, the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon’s Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword stopped dead in front of Cheongpung’s chest.

[P101]
*Crack.*

[P102]
The Sword Energy that had poured from it in torrents only moments ago had vanished. Hairline fractures spread like a spiderweb across the straight, snow-white blade.

[P103]
The Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon stared at his cherished sword, and a weak voice slipped from his lips.

[P104]
“Plum blossoms… I see. You are a disciple of Huashan.”

[P105]
Cheongpung jumped and stammered.

[P106]
“N-No, I’m not.”

[P107]
“Well, I suppose it hardly matters.”

[P108]
Resignation—and understanding.

[P109]
The Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon’s arm slowly sank. His Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword shattered into hundreds of fragments that tumbled across the dueling platform.

[P110]
“I concede.”

[P112]

[P113]

“How was I? I did well, right?”

[P115]

[P116]
“Whoa, you scared me. Let’s cut that out.”

[P117]
“Benefactor, I asked how I did.”

[P118]
Was the young man pestering me for an answer really the same person who had just fought?

[P119]
The Invincible Divine Sword had utterly overwhelmed the Willow-Cloud Divine Dragon, one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes and the future of Wudang.

[P120]
Watching the duel had reminded me once again that Cheongpung had long since surpassed the realm of young prodigies.

[P121]
*Was he always this strong?*

[P122]
The higher you climbed, the more of the landscape you could see. The same was true of the mountain called Cheongpung. A year ago, I hadn’t been high enough to see this view.

[P123]
*He’s incredible. It’s almost impossible to believe that all of this comes from natural talent.*

[P124]
His martial prowess was astonishing, but it was nothing compared to his talent.

[P125]
Watching him, even I could almost believe he was a System user.

[P126]
“Benefactor. Why aren’t you answering?”

[P127]
“Are you a child? Do I have to praise you for that too?”

[P128]
Cheongpung muttered with a slightly downcast expression.

[P129]
“Grandpa always told me I did well…”

[P130]
“That’s between you and him.”

[P131]
I had deliberately answered him curtly when a voice suddenly popped up from somewhere.

[P132]
“Wow, that was a great duel, friend!”

[P133]
Cheongpung’s face lit up as he turned.

[P134]
“Jongni Chu!”

[P135]
“Oh! You remember me, friend!”

[P136]
“Of course I remember you, sir. I mean—of course I do!”

[P137]
“……”

[P138]
*What a pair of fucking idiots.*

[P139]
I silently watched Jongni Chu and Cheongpung embrace and laugh together. Then a thought occurred to me.

[P140]
“Wait. You two.”

[P141]
“Hm? What is it?”

[P142]
“Why?”

[P143]
“Aren’t you each other’s next opponents?”

[P144]
They stared blankly at each other, then gasped.

[P145]
“T-That’s right!”

[P146]
“I-I see. You’re my next opponent, Kang Pung.”

[P147]
I could already hear their friendship cracking.

[P148]
I clicked my tongue as they awkwardly pulled apart.

[P149]
*Well, the result is more or less obvious anyway.*

[P150]
As with everything else, luck played a part in the Star-Array Grand Banquet. In that respect, Jongni Chu had been blessed by the heavens.

[P151]
For some reason, he had kept drawing middling opponents and made it all the way to the semifinals.

[P152]
Of course, the opponents he had defeated only seemed middling to me. They had all been comparable to Jongni Chu or even stronger.

[P153]
*And apparently he even got a bye yesterday.*

[P154]
From what I’d heard, Jongni Chu’s quarterfinal opponent had suffered a severe injury and withdrawn.

[P155]
Whatever else one might say about him, the bastard’s luck was phenomenal.

[P156]
*Still, making it to the semifinals is no small feat.*

[P157]
Cheongpung wasn’t someone who could be defeated through luck. Perhaps they knew that too, because they exchanged a few words with regretful expressions.

[P158]
“I’ll go easy on you. No, I mean…I’ll go easy on you, friend.”

[P159]
“If you would, I’d be grateful. Please do.”

[P160]
One openly promised to go easy on the other, while the other thanked him without a shred of pride. Neither of them was in his right mind.

[P161]
I shook my head.

[P162]
“You two childhood friends can settle that yourselves. I’m leaving. I have a prior engagement.”

[P163]
“A prior engagement? But Benefactor, you don’t have any friends.”

[P164]
“What? You have friends besides me?”

[P165]
“……”

[P166]
The saddest part was that I couldn’t deny it.

[P167]
Just as I found myself at a loss for words, the judge’s shout, amplified by internal energy, rang through the arena.

[P168]
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung! Come up to the dueling platform!”

[P169]
“Yes, I’m coming.”

[P170]
Cheongpung and I each had one more step to climb before we could face each other in the finals.

[P171]
I stepped lightly onto the dueling platform and looked at my opponent.

[P172]
“You got lucky too. I never thought you’d make it this far.”

[P173]
My semifinal opponent muttered gloomily.

[P174]
“Our sect’s Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms is one of the five greatest palm techniques under heaven.”

[P175]
“But you’ve only mastered five tenths of it.”

[P176]
“That is correct.”

[P177]
“Then concede.”

[P178]
“If I did, my Master would beat me like a dog on Boknal.[^1]”

[P179]
“Then?”

[P180]
“There is only one path left.”

[P181]
Gung Gibang, the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect, spat out a thick gob of phlegm. He pointed his well-worn bamboo staff at me and continued.

[P182]
“Our sect’s Dog-Beating Staff Technique is the greatest under heaven. I’ll beat you senseless like a back-alley dog.”

[P183]
“Sure. Go ahead.”

[P184]
Exactly fifteen minutes later, Gung Gibang clung to my calf, both eyes swollen, and shouted,

[P185]
“I’ve only mastered five tenths of the Dog-Beating Staff Technique!”

[P186]
“……”

[P187]
*Why was this bastard stuck at five-tenths mastery with everything?*

[P188]
As I tossed aside the bamboo staff, now split in two, the judge lowered the flag.

[P189]
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung advances to the finals!”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;

Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 253

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃253화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|쉭!
  6|
  7|기수식(起手式) 따위는 없었다. 비무의 시작을 알리는 깃발이 올라가기 무섭게 두 사람은 서로를 향해 쇄도했다.
  8|
  9|그리고 십여 장의 거리가 순식간에 좁혀진 그 순간, 유운신룡의 허리춤에서부터 휘황한 빛줄기가 솟구쳤다.
 10|
 11|‘시작부터 검기를?’
 12|
 13|모든 것에는 장단점이 있는 법.
 14|
 15|검기는 강력한 힘을 발휘하는 대신, 공력 소모가 극심하다.
 16|
 17|유운신룡은 이번 비무에서 장기전이 아니라 속전속결을 택했다.
 18|
 19|슈와악!
 20|
 21|그의 송문고검(松紋古劍)에서 흘러나온 푸른 기운이 청풍의 어깨를 향해 내리그어진다.
 22|
 23|군더더기 없는 일격. 아마 유운신룡이 처음 검을 잡았던 날부터 수없이 휘둘렀던 궤적이었을 것이다.
 24|
 25|하지만…….
 26|
 27|‘내 눈에 보인다는 건, 청풍에게도 마찬가지라는 거지.’
 28|
 29|쾅!
 30|
 31|딱 반걸음 차이. 푸른 검기에 휩싸인 송문고검이 비무대에 작렬했다.
 32|
 33|그러나 유운신룡은 풍부한 경험을 지닌 절정 고수. 그는 예상했다는 듯이 검을 비틀어 청풍의 발목을 베어 갔다.
 34|
 35|“아이코!”
 36|
 37|쉭! 쉬쉬쉭!
 38|
 39|잔망스러운 외침과 함께 검을 피해 낸 청풍이 몸을 뒤틀었다.
 40|
 41|이어서 검기가 맹수의 발톱처럼 사방을 할퀴고 갈라 낸다. 그 궤적에 걸려든 헐렁한 장포 자락이 갈기갈기 찢어져 흩날렸다.
 42|
 43|그 광경에 군중들 사이에서는 비명과 탄성이 흘렀다.
 44|
 45|“꺄악!”
 46|
 47|“헉!”
 48|
 49|하지만 내게는 똑똑히 보인다. 생채기 하나 나지 않은 청풍의 몸과 입가에 매달린 웃음이.
 50|
 51|녀석은 즐기고 있었다. 춤을 추듯 산들거리는 몸놀림으로 검격에서 벗어난 청풍이 활짝 웃으며 박수를 쳤다.
 52|
 53|“와아! 방금 그거 태청검법(太淸劍法)이죠?”
 54|
 55|“마, 맞소.”
 56|
 57|엉겁결에 대답한 유운신룡은 어안이 벙벙한 얼굴이었다.
 58|
 59|그뿐만 아니라 누구라도 그랬을 것이다. 이게 뭐야, 방금 저놈이 어떻게 피한 거지? 그런 생각들로 머리가 꽉 차 있을 것이 분명했다.
 60|
 61|“검로가 되게 재밌다. 혹시 태극혜검(太極慧劍)은 안 익히셨어요?”
 62|
 63|“그건 왜…….”

[P125]
Watching him, even I could almost believe he was a System user.

[P126]
“Benefactor. Why aren’t you answering?”

[P127]
“Are you a child? Do I have to praise you for that too?”

[P128]
Cheongpung muttered with a slightly downcast expression.

[P129]
“Grandpa always told me I did well…”

[P130]
“That’s between you and him.”

[P131]
I had deliberately answered him curtly when a voice suddenly popped up from somewhere.

[P132]
“Wow, that was a great duel, friend!”

[P133]
Cheongpung’s face lit up as he turned.

[P134]
“Jongni Chu!”

[P135]
“Oh! You remember me, friend!”

[P136]
“Of course I remember you, sir. I mean—of course I do!”

[P137]
“……”

[P138]
*What a pair of fucking idiots.*

[P139]
I silently watched Jongni Chu and Cheongpung embrace and laugh together. Then a thought occurred to me.

[P140]
“Wait. You two.”

[P141]
“Hm? What is it?”

[P142]
“Why?”

[P143]
“Aren’t you each other’s next opponents?”

[P144]
They stared blankly at each other, then gasped.

[P145]
“T-That’s right!”

[P146]
“I-I see. You’re my next opponent, Kang Pung.”

[P147]
I could already hear their friendship cracking.

[P148]
I clicked my tongue as they awkwardly pulled apart.

[P149]
*Well, the result is more or less obvious anyway.*

[P150]
As with everything else, luck played a part in the Star-Array Grand Banquet. In that respect, Jongni Chu had been blessed by the heavens.

[P151]
For some reason, he had kept drawing middling opponents and made it all the way to the semifinals.

[P152]
Of course, the opponents he had defeated only seemed middling to me. They had all been comparable to Jongni Chu or even stronger.

[P153]
*And apparently he even got a bye yesterday.*

[P154]
From what I’d heard, Jongni Chu’s quarterfinal opponent had suffered a severe injury and withdrawn.

[P155]
Whatever else one might say about him, the bastard’s luck was phenomenal.

[P156]
*Still, making it to the semifinals is no small feat.*

[P157]
Cheongpung wasn’t someone who could be defeated through luck. Perhaps they knew that too, because they exchanged a few words with regretful expressions.

[P158]
“I’ll go easy on you. No, I mean…I’ll go easy on you, friend.”

[P159]
“If you would, I’d be grateful. Please do.”

[P160]
One openly promised to go easy on the other, while the other thanked him without a shred of pride. Neither of them was in his right mind.

[P161]
I shook my head.

[P162]
“You two childhood friends can settle that yourselves. I’m leaving. I have a prior engagement.”

[P163]
“A prior engagement? But Benefactor, you don’t have any friends.”

[P164]
“What? You have friends besides me?”

[P165]
“……”

[P166]
The saddest part was that I couldn’t deny it.

[P167]
Just as I found myself at a loss for words, the judge’s shout, amplified by internal energy, rang through the arena.

[P168]
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung! Come up to the dueling platform!”

[P169]
“Yes, I’m coming.”

[P170]
Cheongpung and I each had one more step to climb before we could face each other in the finals.

[P171]
I stepped lightly onto the dueling platform and looked at my opponent.

[P172]
“You got lucky too. I never thought you’d make it this far.”

[P173]
My semifinal opponent muttered gloomily.

[P174]
“Our sect’s Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms is one of the five greatest palm techniques under heaven.”

[P175]
“But you’ve only mastered five tenths of it.”

[P176]
“That is correct.”

[P177]
“Then concede.”

[P178]
“If I did, my Master would beat me like a dog on Boknal.[^1]”

[P179]
“Then?”

[P180]
“There is only one path left.”

[P181]
Gung Gibang, the Successor Beggar of the Beggars’ Sect, spat out a thick gob of phlegm. He pointed his well-worn bamboo staff at me and continued.

[P182]
“Our sect’s Dog-Beating Staff Technique is the greatest under heaven. I’ll beat you senseless like a back-alley dog.”

[P183]
“Sure. Go ahead.”

[P184]
Exactly fifteen minutes later, Gung Gibang clung to my calf, both eyes swollen, and shouted,

[P185]
“I’ve only mastered five tenths of the Dog-Beating Staff Technique!”

[P186]
“……”

[P187]
*Why was this bastard stuck at five-tenths mastery with everything?*

[P188]
As I tossed aside the bamboo staff, now split in two, the judge lowered the flag.

[P189]
“Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung advances to the finals!”

[P190]
[^1]: Boknal refers to the hottest days of the Korean summer, traditionally associated with eating dog meat.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
